verifications.claim: Artemis I completed in November 2022.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'launched... on November 16, 2022, and... returning to Earth on December 11.' R5: 'Artemis I (November 16, 2022)' refers to launch.
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm launch in November 2022 but return/splashdown in December 2022; claim incorrectly states completion in November.

verifications.claim: Artemis I was an uncrewed flight test of the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis I was an uncrewed flight test of the Space Launch System and the Orion spacecraft.' R2: 'Artemis I was the first... test of the SLS, Orion.'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state Artemis I as uncrewed test of SLS.

verifications.claim: Artemis I was an uncrewed flight test of the Orion capsule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis I was an uncrewed flight test of the Space Launch System and the Orion spacecraft.' R7: 'Artemis I (2022) was an uncrewed test of the... Orion capsule.'
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported by sources naming Orion as part of uncrewed Artemis I test.

verifications.claim: Artemis I orbited the Moon to verify systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'It... orbited the Moon before returning to Earth' to improve function for crewed flights. R2: 'Artemis I... to lunar orbit.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm lunar orbit for system verification/testing.

verifications.claim: Artemis II launched on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Launch date April 1, 2026, 22:35:12 UTC.' R5: 'Artemis II (April 1, 2026).' R8: 'Artemis 2 launched on 1 April 2026.'
verifications.reasoning: Exact date confirmed across multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed flight of the Artemis program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II will be the first crewed flight of the program.' R4: 'first crewed flight of the NASA-led Artemis program.'
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as first crewed Artemis mission.

verifications.claim: Astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen are the Artemis II crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'U.S. astronauts Reid Wiseman (commander), Victor Glover (pilot), and Christina Koch (mission specialist), and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen.' R4: 'Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, Jeremy Hansen.'
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew named in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is conducting a 10-day flyby.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Their 10-day mission will also include... flyby of the Moon.' R4: 'Mission duration9 days, 1 hour... (approximately 10 days).' R10: '10-day mission around the Moon.'
verifications.reasoning: Described as ~10-day lunar flyby mission; precise duration slightly under 10 days but commonly referred to as 10-day.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is testing life support.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'perform a flyby... include scientific experiments.' R4: 'crew evaluated life support and other critical spacecraft systems.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly mention life support testing during mission.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is breaking crewed distance records.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'set the record for human distance from Earth, 252,756 miles... breaking Apollo 13's record.' R9: 'farthest than any humans have ever traveled before.'
verifications.reasoning: Directly states breaking distance record from Apollo 13.

verifications.claim: Artemis III is targeted for mid-2027.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Artemis III Scheduled for 2027.' R5: 'Artemis III (mid-2027)'
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify mid-2027 target.

verifications.claim: Artemis III is planned to be the first mission to land astronauts on the lunar South Pole.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'test... in Earth orbit on Artemis III, before landing astronauts at the south pole on subsequent missions.' R5: 'Artemis III... test HLS in Earth orbit.' R2: 'first Artemis lunar landing' on IV.
verifications.reasoning: Sources state Artemis III is Earth orbit test; first South Pole landing on later missions like IV.

verifications.claim: Artemis III is planned to utilize SpaceX Starship as a commercial lander.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'test one or both commercial landers from SpaceX and Blue Origin.' R5: 'rendezvous... with... SpaceX's Starship HLS and Blue Origin's Blue Moon.'
verifications.reasoning: Planned to test Starship HLS (among options) in Earth orbit.

verifications.claim: Artemis IV is targeted for early 2028.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'NASA continues to target early 2028.' R5: 'Artemis IV (early 2028)'
verifications.reasoning: Exact target confirmed.

verifications.claim: Artemis IV is planned to deliver crew to the lunar surface.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'first Artemis lunar landing... crew will transfer... to a commercial lunar lander for... descent to the Moon’s surface.' R5: 'first crewed lunar landing.'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly planned as first crewed lunar landing.

verifications.claim: Artemis IV is planned to begin assembly of the Gateway lunar space station.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R5: 'Lunar Gateway program was cancelled in March 2026.' R2: Artemis IV 'lunar landing'; no Gateway mention. R4: Gateway cancelled.
verifications.reasoning: Gateway cancelled; Artemis IV now focused on lunar landing, not Gateway assembly.

verifications.claim: Artemis V is targeted for late 2020s.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'late 2028.' R5: 'Artemis V (late 2028)'
verifications.reasoning: 2028 fits 'late 2020s'; directly supported.

verifications.claim: The Artemis program uses the SLS rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orion will launch atop the Space Launch System (SLS).' R5: 'SLS rocket carrying an Orion spacecraft.'
verifications.reasoning: Core element of program.

verifications.claim: The SLS rocket is 15% more powerful than the Apollo-era Saturn V.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The SLS rocket produces 15% more thrust than the Saturn V rocket that launched the Apollo spacecraft to the Moon.'
verifications.reasoning: Exact figure and comparison stated.

verifications.claim: The Artemis program uses the Orion spacecraft to transport crews.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orion spacecraft... to transport four astronauts to and from the vicinity of the Moon.' R2: 'Orion... carry and sustain the crew on Artemis missions.'
verifications.reasoning: Primary crew vehicle for program.
